English R1B · Reading and Composition

An Octopus

《一只章鱼》

Marianne Moore

1924195 行逐行对照

Marianne Moore（玛丽安·摩尔），“An Octopus”（《一只章鱼》），1924 年发表于 The Dial，同年收入诗集 Observations。左栏英文原文，右栏逐行中文。标题本身就是第一句的开头：“An Octopus / of ice”——“一只章鱼 / 冰做的”，这只“章鱼”指雷尼尔山（Mount Rainier，旧称塔科马山 Mount Tacoma；诗中称 Big Snow Mountain“大雪山”）及其向四面伸展的冰川。诗中大量引号内的文字是摩尔从国家公园手册、旅游指南、报刊、书籍中摘来的原句。课程 PDF 为网页打印稿，长行被折行处已按原诗合并为一行，英文直引号改为弯引号，连字符误代的破折号改回“—”。

An Octopus一只章鱼

课程 PDF 第 1 页
of ice. Deceptively reserved and flat,冰做的。貌似矜持而平坦——却是假象，
it lies “in grandeur and in mass”它躺卧着，“宏伟而厚重”，
beneath a sea of shifting snow-dunes;在一片流移的雪丘之海下；
dots of cyclamen-red and maroon on its clearly defined pseudo-podia仙客来红与栗色的斑点，点缀在它轮廓分明的伪足上，
made of glass that will bend—a much needed invention—那伪足由会弯曲的玻璃制成——一项亟需的发明——
comprising twenty-eight ice-fields from fifty to five hundred feet thick,由二十八片冰原组成，厚五十至五百英尺不等，
of unimagined delicacy.精巧得超乎想象。
“Picking periwinkles from the cracks”“从裂缝里拣食滨螺”，
or killing prey with the concentric crushing rigor of the python,或以蟒蛇那层层收紧的碾压之力扼杀猎物，
it hovers forward “spider fashion它向前浮移，“像蜘蛛那样
on its arms” misleading like lace;用腕足行走”，如蕾丝般迷惑人；
its “ghostly pallor changing它那“幽灵般的苍白
to the green metallic tinge of an anemone-starred pool.”渐变为缀满海葵的水潭那金属般的绿色光泽。”
The fir-trees, in “the magnitude of their root systems,”冷杉，凭着“它们根系的宏大”，
rise aloof from these maneuvers “creepy to behold,”超然耸立于这些“看着就令人发毛”的蠕动之上，
austere specimens of our American royal families,我们美国王室家族中的严峻标本，
“each like the shadow of the one beside it.“每一棵都像身旁那棵的影子。
The rock seems frail compared with the dark energy of life,”与生命的幽暗能量相比，岩石显得脆弱，”
its vermilion and onyx and manganese-blue interior expensiveness它那朱红、缟玛瑙与锰蓝色的内里的奢华
left at the mercy of the weather;任凭风雨处置；
“stained transversely by iron where the water drips down,”“在滴水之处被铁质横向染出条纹，”
recognized by its plants and its animals.凭着它的植物与动物而被辨认。
Completing a circle,绕完一圈，
you have been deceived into thinking that you have progressed,你却被骗得以为自己已经前进，
under the polite needles of the larches在落叶松彬彬有礼的针叶之下，
“hung to filter, not to intercept the sunlight”—那针叶“垂挂着是为了过滤阳光，而非拦截阳光”——
met by tightly wattled spruce-twigs迎面是紧密交织的云杉细枝，
“conformed to an edge like clipped cypress“修整成一道边缘，如同剪齐的柏树，
as if no branch could penetrate the cold beyond its company”;仿佛没有一根枝条能穿透同伴之外的寒冷”；
and dumps of gold and silver ore enclosing The Goat’s Mirror—还有成堆的金矿银矿，环抱着“山羊之镜”——
that lady-fingerlike depression in the shape of the left human foot,那手指饼干般的凹陷，形如一只人的左脚，
which prejudices you in favor of itself它让你先入为主地偏爱它，
before you have had time to see the others;在你还来不及看见其他湖泊之前；
its indigo, pea-green, blue-green, and turquoise,它的靛蓝、豌豆绿、蓝绿与绿松石色，
from a hundred to two hundred feet deep,深一百至二百英尺，
“merging in irregular patches in the middle of the lake“在湖心交融成不规则的色块，
where, like gusts of a storm在那里，像一阵阵风暴
obliterating the shadows of the fir-trees, the wind makes lanes of ripples.”抹去冷杉的倒影，风吹出一道道涟漪的小径。”
课程 PDF 第 2 页
What spot could have merits of equal importance还有什么地方能具有同等重要的优点，
for bears, elks, deer, wolves, goats, and ducks?供熊、麋鹿、鹿、狼、山羊和野鸭栖身？
Pre-empted by their ancestors,这里早已被它们的祖先占据，
this is the property of the exacting porcupine,是挑剔的豪猪的产业，
and of the rat “slipping along to its burrow in the swamp也是老鼠的——它“溜回沼泽中的洞穴，
or pausing on high ground to smell the heather”;或在高地上停下来嗅闻石楠”；
of “thoughtful beavers也是“深思熟虑的河狸”的——
making drains which seem the work of careful men with shovels,”“它们挖出的水渠，仿佛出自手持铁锹的细心人，”
and of the bears inspecting unexpectedly也是熊的——它们出人意料地巡视
ant-hills and berry-bushes.蚁丘和浆果丛。
Composed of calcium gems and alabaster pillars,由钙质宝石与雪花石膏柱构成，
topaz, tourmaline crystals and amethyst quartz,黄玉、电气石晶体与紫水晶石英，
their den is somewhere else, concealed in the confusion它们的巢穴却在别处，藏匿于一片混乱之中——
of “blue forests thrown together with marble and jasper and agate“蓝色的森林与大理石、碧玉和玛瑙胡乱堆在一起，
as if the whole quarries had been dynamited.”仿佛整座采石场都被炸药炸开过。”
And farther up, in a stag-at-bay position再往高处，摆出困兽回身相抗的姿态，
as a scintillating fragment of these terrible stalagmites,像这些可怕石笋中一块闪烁的碎片，
stands the goat,站着那只山羊，
its eye fixed on the waterfall which never seems to fall—目光凝定在那道仿佛永不落下的瀑布上——
an endless skein swayed by the wind,一束被风摇曳的无尽丝绞，
immune to force of gravity in the perspective of the peaks.在群峰的透视中不受重力支配。
A special antelope一种特别的羚羊，
acclimated to “grottoes from which issue penetrating draughts适应了“那些吹出刺骨穿堂风的岩洞，
which make you wonder why you came,”让你纳闷自己为何要来，”
it stands its ground它坚守着自己的阵地，
on cliffs the color of the clouds, of petrified white vapor—在云色的悬崖上，在石化的白色雾气上——
black feet, eyes, nose, and horns, engraved on dazzling ice-fields,黑色的蹄、眼、鼻与角，镌刻在耀眼的冰原上，
the ermine body on the crystal peak;貂白的身躯立于水晶般的峰顶；
the sun kindling its shoulders to maximum heat like acetylene,太阳把它的肩头烧到极热，如乙炔焰，
dyeing them white—将它们染成白色——
upon this antique pedestal,在这古老的基座之上，
“a mountain with those graceful lines which prove it a volcano,”“一座山，那些优雅的线条证明它是一座火山，”
its top a complete cone like Fujiyama’s它的山顶曾是一个完整的圆锥，如富士山一般，
till an explosion blew it off.直到一次爆发把它掀掉。
Distinguished by a beauty以一种美而著称——
of which “the visitor dare never fully speak at home对这种美，“游人回到家中永远不敢尽情讲述，
for fear of being stoned as an impostor,”唯恐被当作骗子而遭石块砸打，”
Big Snow Mountain is the home of a diversity of creatures:大雪山是形形色色生灵的家园：
those who “have lived in hotels那些“曾住过旅馆，
but who now live in camps—who prefer to”;如今却住在营地里——而且宁愿如此”的人；
the mountain guide evolving from the trapper,由捕兽人演变而来的登山向导，
“in two pairs of trousers, the outer one older,“穿着两条裤子，外面那条旧些，
wearing slowly away from the feet to the knees”;从脚边一路慢慢磨损到膝盖”；
“the nine-striped chipmunk“九道条纹的花栗鼠
running with unmammal-like agility along a log”;以不像哺乳动物的敏捷沿着原木奔跑”；
the water ouzel河乌
课程 PDF 第 3 页
with “its passion for rapids and high-pressured falls,”怀着“它对急流与高压瀑布的热情，”
building under the arch of some tiny Niagara;在某座小小尼亚加拉的拱下筑巢；
the white-tailed ptarmigan “in winter solid white,白尾雷鸟，“冬天通体雪白，
feeding on heather-bells and alpine buckwheat”;以石楠铃花与高山荞麦为食”；
and the eleven eagles of the west,还有西部的十一种鹰，
“fond of the spring fragrance and the winter colors,”“喜爱春天的芬芳与冬天的色彩，”
used to the unegoistic action of the glaciers习惯了冰川那毫无私心的运动
and “several hours of frost every midsummer night.”和“每个仲夏夜里几个小时的霜冻。”
“They make a nice appearance, don’t they,”“它们看上去挺体面，不是吗，”
happy seeing nothing?快乐得什么也看不见？
Perched on treacherous lava and pumice—栖身于危险的熔岩和浮石之上——
those unadjusted chimney-pots and cleavers那些未经调整的烟囱帽与劈刀般的岩峰，
which stipulate “names and addresses of persons to notify它们要求登记“需通知者的姓名与地址，
in case of disaster”—以备发生灾难之时”——
they hear the roar of ice and supervise the water它们听着冰的轰鸣，监看着流水
winding slowly through the cliffs,在悬崖间缓缓蜿蜒，
the road “climbing like the thread而道路“攀升起来，像那条
which forms the groove around a snail-shell,在蜗牛壳上绕出凹槽的螺纹，
doubling back and forth until where snow begins, it ends.”来回折返，直到积雪开始之处，它便终止。”
No “deliberate wide-eyed wistfulness” is here这里没有“刻意的、睁大眼睛的怅惘”，
among the boulders sunk in ripples and white water在沉入涟漪与白浪的巨石之间，
where “when you hear the best wild music of the forest在那里，“当你听到森林里最好的野性音乐，
it is sure to be a marmot,”那必定是一只旱獭，”
the victim on some slight observatory,它在某个小小的瞭望台上，成了
of “a struggle between curiosity and caution,”“好奇与谨慎之间的一场挣扎”的牺牲品，
inquiring what has scared it:探问是什么惊吓了它：
a stone from the moraine descending in leaps,是一块从冰碛上跳跃而下的石头，
another marmot, or the spotted ponies with glass eyes,是另一只旱獭，还是那些长着玻璃眼睛的花斑小马，
brought up on frosty grass and flowers吃着带霜的草和花长大，
and rapid draughts of ice-water.大口喝着冰水。
Instructed none knows how, to climb the mountain,不知是谁教会它们攀登这座山——
by business men who require for recreation是那些为了消遣
three hundred and sixty-five holidays in the year,一年需要三百六十五天假期的商人，
these conspicuously spotted little horses are peculiar;这些斑点显眼的小马很是奇特；
hard to discern among the birch-trees, ferns, and lily-pads,在白桦、蕨类与睡莲叶间难以辨认，
avalanche lilies, Indian paint-brushes,雪崩百合、印第安画笔花，
bear’s ears and kittentails,熊耳草和小猫尾草，
and miniature cavalcades of chlorophylless fungi还有一队队不含叶绿素的真菌，像微型的骑兵行列，
magnified in profile on the moss-beds like moonstones in the water;侧影在苔藓床上被放大，如水中的月长石；
the cavalcade of calico competing那花布般的马队，竞相媲美于
with the original American menagerie of styles美洲原有的种种风格的动物园，
among the white flowers of the rhododendron surmounting rigid leaves在杜鹃花高踞于僵硬叶片之上的白色花朵间，
upon which moisture works its alchemy,湿气在那些叶片上施展它的炼金术，
transmuting verdure into onyx.把青翠转化为缟玛瑙。
“Like happy souls in Hell,” enjoying mental difficulties,“像地狱中快乐的灵魂”，享受着心智上的难题，
the Greeks希腊人
课程 PDF 第 4 页
amused themselves with delicate behavior以优雅的举止自娱，
because it was “so noble and fair”;因为那是“如此高贵而美好”；
not practised in adapting their intelligence他们不习惯让自己的才智
to eagle-traps and snow-shoes,去适应捕鹰器和雪鞋，
to alpenstocks and other toys contrived by those适应登山杖以及其他玩具——那些玩具出自
“alive to the advantage of invigorating pleasures.”“深知令人振奋的乐趣之益处”的人之手。
Bows, arrows, oars, and paddles, for which trees provide the wood,弓、箭、桨与划子，树木为之提供木材，
in new countries more eloquent than elsewhere—在新的国度里比别处更加雄辩——
augmenting the assertion that, essentially humane,更增强了这样一个论断：本质上合乎人道，
“the forest affords wood for dwellings and by its beauty“森林为住所提供木材，并以其美
stimulates the moral vigor of its citizens.”激发其公民的道德活力。”
The Greeks liked smoothness, distrusting what was back希腊人喜欢光滑，不信任藏在
of what could not be clearly seen,无法看清之物背后的东西，
resolving with benevolent conclusiveness,以仁慈的决断解决
“complexities which still will be complexities“那些复杂之事，只要世界还存在，
as long as the world lasts”;就仍将是复杂之事”；
ascribing what we clumsily call happiness,把我们笨拙地称作幸福的东西，
to “an accident or a quality,归因于“一种偶性或一种性质，
a spiritual substance or the soul itself,一种精神实体或灵魂本身，
an act, a disposition, or a habit,一种行为、一种倾向或一种习性，
or a habit infused, to which the soul has been persuaded,或一种被灌注的习性，灵魂已被说服接受它，
or something distinct from a habit, a power”—或某种有别于习性的东西，一种能力”——
such power as Adam had and we are still devoid of.那种亚当曾拥有、而我们至今仍缺乏的能力。
“Emotionally sensitive, their hearts were hard”;“情感敏锐，他们的心却是硬的”；
their wisdom was remote他们的智慧相去甚远，
from that of these odd oracles of cool official sarcasm,远离这些冷峻官方讽刺的古怪神谕——
upon this game preserve在这片禁猎保护区上，
where “guns, nets, seines, traps, and explosives,那里“枪支、网具、围网、陷阱与爆炸物，
hired vehicles, gambling and intoxicants are prohibited;租用的车辆、赌博与酒类一律禁止；
disobedient persons being summarily removed违者将被立即驱逐，
and not allowed to return without permission in writing.”且未经书面许可不得返回。”
It is self-evident不言自明的是，
that it is frightful to have everything afraid of one;让万物都怕你，是件可怕的事；
that one must do as one is told人必须照吩咐行事，
and eat rice, prunes, dates, raisins, hardtack, and tomatoes吃米饭、西梅、椰枣、葡萄干、硬饼干和番茄，
if one would “conquer the main peak of Mount Tacoma,”如果你想“征服塔科马山的主峰”，
this fossil flower concise without a shiver,这朵化石之花，简洁而毫不战栗，
intact when it is cut,切开时依然完好，
damned for its sacrosanct remoteness—因它神圣不可侵犯的疏远而遭诅咒——
like Henry James “damned by the public for decorum”;就像亨利·詹姆斯“因得体而遭公众诅咒”；
not decorum, but restraint;不是得体，而是克制；
it is the love of doing hard things正是对做难事的热爱
that rebuffed and wore them out—a public out of sympathy with neatness.挫败并耗尽了他们——一群对整洁毫无同情的公众。
Neatness of finish! Neatness of finish!收尾的整洁！收尾的整洁！
Relentless accuracy is the nature of this octopus无情的精确是这只章鱼的本性，
with its capacity for fact.它有着容纳事实的能力。
课程 PDF 第 5 页
“Creeping slowly as with meditated stealth,“缓缓爬行，如怀着蓄谋的隐秘，
its arms seeming to approach from all directions,”它的腕足仿佛从四面八方逼近，”
it receives one under winds that “tear the snow to bits它在风中接纳来人，那风“把雪撕成碎片，
and hurl it like a sandblast像喷砂一样将它抛掷出去，
shearing off twigs and loose bark from the trees.”削去树上的细枝与松动的树皮。”
Is “tree” the word for these things“树”这个字眼配得上这些东西吗——
“flat on the ground like vines”?“像藤蔓一样平贴在地上”？
some “bent in a half circle with branches on one side有的“弯成半圆，枝条只长在一侧，
suggesting dust-brushes, not trees;让人想起掸子，而非树木；
some finding strength in union, forming little stunted groves有的在联合中寻得力量，形成矮小的树丛，
their flattened mats of branches shrunk in trying to escape”它们扁平的枝垫在试图逃离时缩拢了”
from the hard mountain “planed by ice and polished by the wind”—逃离那座坚硬的山——“被冰刨平，被风磨光”——
the white volcano with no weather side;那没有迎风面的白色火山；
the lightning flashing at its base,闪电在它的山脚闪烁，
rain falling in the valleys, and snow falling on the peak—雨落在山谷里，雪落在峰顶上——
the glassy octopus symmetrically pointed,这只玻璃般的章鱼，对称地挺出尖角，
its claw cut by the avalanche它的一只爪被雪崩截断，
“with a sound like the crack of a rifle,“伴着一声如步枪爆响的声音，
in a curtain of powdered snow launched like a waterfall.”在一道如瀑布般泻下的粉雪帘幕中。”

与课程 PDF 的出入：PDF 在 “and eat rice, prunes, dates, raisins, hardtack, and tomatoes” 之后漏了一行，已据 1924 年版补入 “if one would ‘conquer the main peak of Mount Tacoma,’”（第 166 行）。另据原诗改正 PDF 中的五处笔误：happy see → happy seeing，it stands it ground → its ground，their den in → is，stunted grooves → groves，“planned by ice” → “planed by ice”。
